gallery.title: Gallery
gallery.subtitle: Twenty photographs
gallery.intro: Wing A, Of Jack: portraits of Jack. Wing B, By Jack: photographs by Jack. Hung chronologically within each wing. No quality photographs from November to December 2022 were found in the library, so the earliest work is August 2023.

wings.name: Of Jack
wings.description: Portraits of Jack, August 2023 to October 2026. A12, The Bund at Night, is the centrepiece and should be displayed larger than the rest.

wings.name: By Jack
wings.description: Photographs taken by Jack, Jack behind the camera, August 2023 to August 2026.

works.title: The Bund at Night
works.description: Smiling, black polo and watch, the Oriental Pearl Tower and the Lujiazui skyline across the Huangpu River, a boat lit blue on the water.
works.curatorialNote: The masterpiece of the collection and its largest print: the highest resolution in the set, the warmest light, the subject dead centre. Every other portrait in this wing is, in some sense, walking toward or away from this one.

works.title: No. 5, Blue Door
works.location: West Village / Washington Square, New York
works.description: Full body in black, hand on the handle of a blue door numbered 5, beige stucco, a purple flower box above.
works.curatorialNote: The strongest full-body street portrait in the collection: one door, one colour, one figure. It needs nothing else in the frame and has nothing else in the frame.

works.title: Gold Pyramid, Atlanta Night
works.description: Selfie in black T-shirt, backpack with a plush-toy strap, peace sign, the gold-lit pyramid top of Bank of America Plaza behind at night.
works.curatorialNote: The finale of Wing A. Atlanta answers Shanghai from across the room: another tower lit at night, another grin, home turf this time.

works.title: Raffles, in White
works.description: The white colonial facade of Raffles Hotel, green lawn, grey sky, classical symmetry.
works.curatorialNote: The photographer's earliest exhibited work: a study in whiteness and order, taken straight on, as the building insists.

works.title: Departure, Changi
works.description: Through an airplane window: a Singapore Airlines tail and wing over the tarmac, pale teal sky, the window frame kept in shot.
works.curatorialNote: Every travel collection needs its leaving picture. The frame inside the frame is the whole composition, and it is a good one.

works.title: The Wavy Tower
works.location: High Line, New York (520 West 28th Street)
works.description: The wavy glass Zaha Hadid tower above High Line planting, blue sky.
works.curatorialNote: The best architecture of 2023 in this set, and the highest-resolution OnePlus frame. The building ripples; the photograph stands still.

works.title: Totality, Vermont
works.description: Diamond-ring totality in a twilight sky over a dark field and tree line, spectators silhouetted below.
works.curatorialNote: The one unrepeatable work in the exhibition. Dozens of near-identical sun-dots were culled; this wide frame, with the field and the crowd gone dark, is the keeper.

works.title: Chicago, from the Air at Night
works.description: A grid of city lights and cloud seen from above at night, the window frame at the edge.
works.curatorialNote: The collection's only aerial. A city reduced to circuitry, which, given the photographer, feels less like a metaphor than a habit of seeing.

works.title: LaSalle Street Bridge
works.description: A steel bridge deck over the Chicago River, glass towers beyond, an overcast sky, the metal grate foreground leading in.
works.curatorialNote: The strongest leading line of 2024. The photograph walks you across the bridge whether you meant to cross or not.

works.title: The Seagull at the Dylan
works.location: The Dylan, Midtown Manhattan, New York
works.description: A rooftop terrace at sunset, a tower under construction with its crane, and a seagull perched on the railing, looking back.
works.curatorialNote: Without the bird, a good skyline. With the bird, the photograph every visitor remembers. The seagull has reviewed the view and found it acceptable.

works.title: Northwestern, from Above
works.description: An elevated view over a lagoon and fountain, campus buildings, Lake Michigan on the horizon.
works.curatorialNote: A campus composed like a map of itself. Hung among the skylines as a reminder that not every horizon in this collection is made of towers.

works.title: Reeds and Rust, Hudson River
works.location: Hudson River Park / Little Island, New York
works.description: The Manhattan skyline across the Hudson, tall reeds and rusty posts in the foreground, blue sky.
works.curatorialNote: Independence Day, photographed quietly. The foreground does the work: weeds and iron first, the famous skyline second.

works.title: Oculus, Golden Hour
works.description: The white ribbed Oculus glowing gold in evening sun, a street crossing and pedestrians, downtown towers around.
works.curatorialNote: The best of several Oculus frames, chosen for the minute the building turns from white to gold. Architecture as sundial.

works.title: The Walkway to Manhattan
works.location: Queensboro Bridge, Hunters Point, New York
works.description: A pedestrian walkway running toward Manhattan's glass towers at sunset, one distant walker, lamps lit.
works.curatorialNote: The strongest leading line in the New York group. One small figure walks the line the photograph draws, which is all the human presence it needs.

works.title: One World Trade, from Jersey City
works.description: The Manhattan skyline across the Hudson, One World Trade Center at centre, a ferry at right, dramatic cloud, sunlit water.
works.curatorialNote: The classic wide Manhattan view, and the best of its kind in the set. Some postcards are postcards because they are true.

works.title: Ohio Street Beach
works.description: A black ornate railing, Lake Michigan, towers to the left, the Navy Pier Ferris wheel distant at right, dramatic cloud.
works.curatorialNote: Chicago given the same treatment as New York in B13, and holding its own. The railing's ironwork is the signature at the bottom of the canvas.

works.title: The Outdoor Screen
works.description: A giant outdoor cinema screen on an angular building, showing a film still of two silhouettes, Chinese text running up its side, blue sky.
works.curatorialNote: A photograph of a screen showing a film: three layers of looking at once. The boldest and strangest image in Wing B, hung proudly.

works.title: West Bund Canopy
works.description: A glass lattice canopy and a curved glass tower, a circular walkway, blue sky.
works.curatorialNote: The strongest Shanghai architecture in the collection, all symmetry and lattice. The photographer's engineering eye, pointed at someone else's engineering.

works.title: Sri Mariamman Temple
works.description: The colourful gopuram tower against blue sky, shophouses along the street, a blue-haired passer-by in the foreground.
works.curatorialNote: The richest colour in the exhibition. Five centuries of temple sculpture, one Singapore street, and a stranger whose hair matches the sky.

works.title: Riverfront, Singapore
works.description: A riverfront promenade, white railings leading the eye to downtown skyscrapers, blue sky and a single contrail.
works.curatorialNote: The closing work. The cleanest cityscape in the set, and the natural end of the walk: railings, river, towers, out.
